title: Al-Mutakabbir, the Supreme in Greatness
hookLine: the Supreme in Greatness, to whom alone greatness belongs, and one human family under it
tomorrow: she said yes. now how do you plan a life you can't see yet?

cards: The acceptance post is drafted: the logo, the confetti, a caption that sounds humble and isn't. Yesterday's question was what's left for pride once you see who mends what. Today's name answers.
Al-Mutakabbir closes that list of names in Surah al-Hashr. Pickthall calls Him the Superb: the Supreme in Greatness, the one to whom greatness belongs.

teach.b: A sacred hadith, in Muslim's collection and Abu Dawud's, puts it as a picture, in paraphrase: greatness is My cloak. Whoever tries to wear it, I'll cast away.
Then the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, defined pride so nobody could miss it, in Sahih Muslim: pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people.
Not nice clothes; he said in the same breath that Allah is beautiful and loves beauty. Looking down on people.
And in words from his farewell, recorded by Ahmad, in paraphrase: your Lord is one and your father is one.
No Arab is above a non-Arab, no non-Arab above an Arab, no red above black, no black above red, except by mindfulness of God. One human family, and greatness belongs to none of it.

teach.h: A WEEK OF NAMES, ALL HIS.
teach.b: That's this week, too: Al-Malik, Al-Quddus, As-Salam, Al-Mu'min, Al-Muhaymin, Al-'Aziz, Al-Jabbar, and now Al-Mutakabbir.
Every one of them His. Something to tell a friend tonight: the Prophet's definition of pride doesn't mention clothes or money; it's about how you look at people.

how: Muslims say Allahu akbar, Allah is greater, at the start of each prayer and through it, and are taught to see humility toward people as part of faith.

o: the Highest, who lives above the seven skies
the Proud, who wants people to fear Him
the Supreme in Greatness, to whom it belongs

games.q: greatness is His — tap the pairs.
p: rejecting truth, looking down on people

s: the Prophet called liking nice clothes a kind of pride
he said Allah is beautiful and loves beauty; pride is rejecting truth and looking down on people.
the farewell words say no Arab is above a non-Arab, except by mindfulness of God
recorded by Ahmad: your Lord is one, and your father is one.

games.q: you made the varsity team and a friend didn't. at lunch, people start joking about how badly he played. what does the Prophet's definition of pride say?
o: pride is looking down on people; skip the joke, and keep your joy.
pride is any happiness about winning; hide that you made the team.
it's only pride if you say it to his face, not behind his back.
games.why: pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people. joy in a good thing isn't it; the joke at his expense is.

practice: Write by hand one thing you're proud of this week. Next to it, write the names of everyone who helped make it happen. For the sit, look at the list and let the credit spread out across it.

wordCard.voice: Al-Mutakabbir: the Supreme in Greatness, to whom alone greatness belongs. Pickthall's word is the Superb.

orig.note: Arabic: the Supreme in Greatness, the One to whom greatness truly belongs.

carryVoice: Your line: greatness is his, and the rest of us stand level under it. Until tomorrow.

sources.ref: Sahih Muslim 2620; Sunan Abi Dawud 4090 (sacred hadith: greatness is My cloak; whoever contends with Me for it, I cast him away)
Sahih Muslim 91 (Allah is beautiful and loves beauty; pride is rejecting the truth and looking down on people)
Musnad Ahmad 23489 (your Lord is one and your father is one; no Arab over a non-Arab, nor non-Arab over an Arab, nor red over black, nor black over red, except by taqwa)
